instructions: AGENTS.md contains the project architecture, tech stack, and conventions. Read it before starting any work. Development follows the issue-driven cycle: user raises requirement → grill-me → create issue → implement → push.

rules.requirement-flow: When the user raises a feature or bug requirement: run /grill-me to clarify scope and decisions, summarize the locked-in decisions, then create a GitHub issue (feature_request or bug_report template) with the summary, show the issue with `gh issue view <N>`, then implement.
rules.issue-linking: Bugfix commits use `fixes #N`. Feature commits use `closes #N`. GitHub auto-closes the issue on push to main.
rules.bug-reporting: If you discover a new bug during development: create a GitHub issue using the bug_report template, read it back with `gh issue view <N>`, then fix it.
rules.plan-mode: Multi-step tasks (2+ modules, architecture changes, new data sources) MUST use /ulw-plan before implementing. Single-file fixes, tests, and doc updates may proceed directly with explore → implement.
rules.local-verify-before-push: Run `cargo nextest run && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check` before every push. All must pass — never push broken code hoping CI catches it.
rules.per-step-verify: After every code change: run `cargo nextest run` and ensure `lsp_diagnostics` is clean on changed files. Failures must be fixed before continuing.
rules.push-after-issue: Push to main immediately after completing each issue. Do not batch commits across multiple issues.
rules.atomic-commits: Commit each logical unit separately. One commit = one purpose (fix, feat, test, refactor). Never mix unrelated changes. Use `.gitmessage` template format.
rules.branching: Trunk-based: push directly to `main`. No feature branches, no PRs for solo development.
rules.doc-sync: When changing architecture, data flow, symbol format, config schema, or adding new kb-worthy patterns: update both AGENTS.md and the relevant kb/ file.
rules.test-first: Any new module or behavior change must include tests (rstest + #[tokio::test]). Tests must pass before marking work complete.
rules.no-type-escape: Never use `as any`, `@ts-ignore`, or `unwrap()` in production code. Use `.expect(msg)` or proper error handling.
rules.code-style: Match existing codebase conventions: Rust edition 2024, thiserror for errors, async-trait for trait async fns, tracing for logging.
